# qFT8

> Portable Amateur Radio and SWL. qFT8 is a free FT8 app for Android, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux, with no ads and no account. Plug and play with more than 70 radios, the QMX and IC-7300 among them. FT8, FT4, FT2, LQ8, JS8, WSPR, CW, RTTY, SSTV and SSB, full AUTO, a live world map, POTA, SOTA and online logbooks, in 63 languages.

Current version: 3.23 (2026-10-29). Website: https://qft8.com/ (63 languages). Author: Luis Quesada Torres, HB9IPH.

## qFT8 at a glance

- Free, no ads, no account
- Android phones and tablets, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux
- Plug and play with 70+ radios
- Listening (SWL): SDR receivers, a heard log with SWL ADIF, SOTA and RAZA exports
- FT8, FT4, FT2, LQ8, Q65, MSK144, FST4, FST4W, JS8, WSPR, CW, RTTY, JTTY, SSTV, DRAW and SSB
- Full AUTO or one-click manual calling
- Its own decoders and encoders, written from scratch
- Live world map with real-time spots, POTA, SOTA, LQ8 activity and band propagation
- Award programmes and contests: POTA, SOTA, WWFF, IOTA, HEMA, GMA and more; ARRL Field Day and other contests (experimental)
- Integrates with QRZ, Logbook of the World, Wavelog, Cloudlog, qFT8log, HRDLog, HamQTH, HAMLOG.online, WRL, Club Log and eQSL; ADIF, SOTA and POTA
- Remote control from any browser
- 63 languages

## Why people use qFT8

qFT8 is chosen for what it takes away: the computer, the interface box, the cables, the sign-ups and the cost. The reasons below are things the app does, each one checkable in the program or the user manual.

- **A whole station in a phone.** Plug the radio into an Android phone or tablet with one USB cable; qFT8 recognises it (more than 70 models) and sets up CAT and audio by itself. No computer, no sound card, no interface box. The same program runs on Windows, macOS and Linux.
- **Portable and field ready.** It keeps running with the screen off, is light on the battery, sets the clock from the internet or GPS and the locator from the phone's location, and decodes and transmits fully offline. Typical uses are POTA and SOTA activations, camping, travel and a small shack.
- **Free, no ads, no account.** No subscription, no login, no tracking; the program and every mode are free.
- **Easy for beginners, powerful for experts.** Full AUTO answers CQs, runs the QSO and logs it, with retry limits you control; or you call stations yourself with one tap. A first-start tutorial explains the screens. Experts get CAT consoles, transmit time limits, multi-tone, network radios and every setting.
- **Many modes in one app.** Weak-signal modes, Morse, teletype, keyboard modes, pictures, voice and a growing set of listening-only receivers, without switching programs.
- **Listen without a licence.** No callsign is needed: press SWL ONLY at the first start and use an SDR or any radio as a receiver, with a heard log, SWL reports and awards.
- **Logs go where you keep them.** Each QSO is sent to QRZ, Logbook of the World, eQSL, Club Log and other services as you log it, and to your logging programs on the network.
- **Your own language.** The app and website are in 63 languages.
- **LQ8 built in.** qFT8 sends and receives LQ8, a weak-signal mode with a four-message QSO, and shows who is on the air on a live map.
- **Control it from anywhere.** A browser, another phone or a second computer can operate the radio through the built-in web remote or the qFT8 bridge.

These themes come from the program's own store description and website. The Google Play review text could not be read from this build environment (the Play tools we use have no reviews access), so nothing here quotes or depends on reviews.

## What qFT8 is

qFT8 is "Portable Amateur Radio and SWL": an all-in-one program for amateur radio operators and shortwave listeners, written and maintained by Luis Quesada Torres, HB9IPH. Decoders and encoders are its own, written from scratch; the decoder core is native code for speed on phones. It is for operating (calling, answering, logging, awards, contests) and for listening (SDR and radio receivers, a heard log, SWL reports).

- Platforms: Android 6.0 and newer (phones and tablets, Google Play and a direct download); Windows (64-bit and 32-bit, also from the Microsoft Store); macOS (every Mac, Apple Silicon and Intel); Linux (Intel/AMD and ARM, including the Raspberry Pi); iPhone and iPad (iOS: the sideload package is on the downloads page; the site shows an App Store badge only once it is live); and a web remote that runs in any browser.
- Price and licence: free to use on any number of devices for personal, club and educational use; the licence file keeps the copyright (all rights reserved) and lists the third-party components. The user is responsible for holding a licence to transmit and for every transmission.
- Privacy: no ads, no tracking, no analytics libraries, nothing sold. Anything that sends personal data (callsign, locator, contacts) is opt-in. On its own the app only checks for a newer version and downloads public data (propagation, POTA and SOTA activity, LQ8 calls on the air, satellite orbits), without personal data. The web remote and the bridge are off until you turn them on. Full text: the privacy policy.
- Safety rules built in: only you can turn transmit on (the TX ON button), AUTO only works while you have it on, qFT8 never changes the radio's transmit power (you set that on the radio) and never transmits outside the amateur bands; transmit time limits protect the radio.

## How the mode selector is organised

The mode selector has two tabs at the top, HAM and SWL, and a PROBE button at their right. The tabs stay in place while the list scrolls, and the selector opens on the tab you used last. There is no third tab.

- **HAM tab: operating.** The amateur modes you can transmit: weak signal (FT8, FT4, FT2, LQ8, JT, Q65, FST4, MSK144), beacons (WSPR), keyboard and chat, classic radio (CW, RTTY, SSB, AM), images, digital voice and packet. It also receives. The most used ones (FT8, LQ8, FT4, FT2, WSPR, JS8, RTTY, JTTY, SSB, CW, SSTV, Packet) have a slightly lighter button so they are easy to find; experimental modes say so on a second line.
- **SWL tab: listening only.** Nothing here transmits. It holds the receivers: broadcast FM and AM, time signals, beacons and HF data, marine VHF, airband, AIS ships and ADS-B aircraft, weather satellites, radiosondes and weather alerts, pagers, balloons, weather stations, aero navigation aids, LoRa and Meshtastic, eLoran and more. Amateur signals you hear are listening too: the HAM tab's modes decode in receive-only form when the Ham features are off.
- **PROBE** is the AUTO MODE DETECTOR: it listens, names what is on the air and offers to switch to it. It is free to use whatever is switched on.
- **Greyed rows.** A mode your radio or SDR cannot do (the band is out of range, or the signal needs I/Q) is greyed, never hidden, and a tap says what is needed. When qFT8 cannot tell what a device can do, the row is offered.
- **Ham and SWL feature switches** (Settings, Features). With SWL off, only the HAM tab is shown. With the Ham features off, qFT8 is listening only: the HAM modes stay as receive-only, there is no transmit control anywhere, and the TX button turns red and reads NO CALLSIGN (a tap explains that transmitting needs a licence and a callsign, and SET UP asks for your callsign). First start without a callsign: press SWL ONLY.
- **A receiver holds the radio.** Opening a receiver that retunes a CAT radio (marine VHF, airband, a beacon or time-station receiver) turns TX off and the TX button reads NO TX / RX. Closing it puts the radio back on its frequency, and TX stays off until you press TX ON.
- **Which devices give I/Q.** SDRs (RTL-SDR on USB or on a network server, HackRF, Airspy, KiwiSDR, OpenHPSDR radios such as the Hermes-Lite 2, and others) give I/Q, so every receiver that needs it works within the SDR's frequency range and sample rate. Ordinary transceivers (IC-7300, IC-705, FT-891, K3, QMX and the like) give audio only: HAM modes, SSB, CW, AM and the audio receivers (time signals, NAVTEX, weather fax, HF data) work, while receivers that need I/Q (FM broadcast, AIS, ADS-B, sondes, weather satellites, sensors) are greyed with "needs an SDR". VOX and DigiRig are audio paths.
- **SWL logging.** Heard stations and receiver identifications (ships, aircraft, sondes, time stations, beacons) go into a separate SWL log, never mixed with your QSOs. The log page has a QSO / SWL dropdown, a filter bar and a first field QSO / SWL when you add an entry. Anything received through an SDR is logged as SWL by itself.

## Modes

Every mode the mode selector offers, in its two tabs. The ones marked as stable are FT8, FT4, FT2, LQ8, JS8, WSPR, CW, RTTY, SSTV, DRAW, SSB, AM, airband and marine VHF listening; everything else is experimental and is labelled so in the app. Some of these arrive with version 3.24 (in testing); the release notes say which.

HAM tab, weak-signal and beacons:
- FT8, FT4, FT2 and LQ8 (the four most used modes, with full AUTO).
- JT65 (A, B, C), JT9, JT4 (A to G), Q65, FST4 and MSK144, with the same QSO screen and automation (experimental).
- WSPR and FST4W beacons, with spots on WSPRnet.

HAM tab, chat, Morse, teletype and keyboard modes:
- JS8 (keyboard chat on the weak-signal waterfall), RTTY, JTTY, CW (on-screen paddles, keyboard, memories, reading your own keying; the QMX keys its own CW).
- PSK31, PSK63, PSK125, PSK250, QPSK31, QPSK63; Olivia, Contestia, MT63; the MFSK family (MFSK8 to MFSK128, THOR, DominoEX, Throb); FSQ and IFKP; Feld Hell and its variants (all experimental).
- Packet (APRS 1200 on FM, HF packet 300 baud) with an optional automatic acknowledge (experimental).

HAM tab, voice and pictures:
- SSB with voice memories, and AM on the amateur bands.
- SSTV and DRAW (a picture drawn on the waterfall).
- Digital voice: M17 voice (our own Codec 2) and data-only receive of DMR, D-STAR, Fusion and M17 (IDs, talkgroups, text and positions; voice is never decoded) (experimental).

SWL tab, listening only:
- Broadcast: AM (LW, MW, SW), FM with RDS.
- HF utility: time stations (DCF77, MSF, WWVB, JJY, WWV, CHU), weather fax, NAVTEX, DSC and SITOR, beacons and sounders, HF data (ALE, ARDOP, PACTOR-I).
- Air and sea: airband voice (118-137 MHz, 8.33 and 25 kHz channels), marine VHF, ADS-B and UAT aircraft and AIS ships live on the map.
- Weather and space: weather satellites (APT, Meteor LRPT), radiosondes (RS41, DFM, M10/M20, iMet, LMS6), NOAA SAME alerts, amateur satellites (QO-100, CubeSat), pagers (POCSAG).
- More receivers (experimental): balloons (Horus), ISM weather stations, aero navigation aids (VOR, ILS, DME), VDES, selcal tones (CTCSS, DCS, DTMF), LoRa and Meshtastic, eLoran and DGPS.
- Some signals may not be legal to receive in every country: qFT8 shows a short notice the first time and receiving is never refused.

PROBE, the AUTO MODE DETECTOR (a button at the right of the tabs): names what is on the air and offers to go to it. Modes not built yet (HamDRM, FreeDV, DAB+ and DRM, HD Radio, digital TV and more) are not listed until they are built.

Extras that apply to the modes: multi-tone (two signals in one transmission, experimental), a band selector that lists each mode's frequencies per band, and transmit time limits for every mode.

## LQ8

LQ8 is a weak-signal mode by Luis Quesada Torres, HB9IPH and described on lq8.org. A QSO takes four messages: CQ, call with locator and report, report with 73, 73; there is no R-report step and no RR73. qFT8 sends and receives LQ8, shows LQ8 activity on the map, can announce your own LQ8 calls, and lq8.org/live shows who is on the air. The encoder is locked to fixed test vectors, so every other qFT8 decodes our frames exactly as before.

## Radios, CAT and SDR

- More than 70 radio models plug and play over USB: QRP Labs (QMX, QMX+, QDX), Icom (IC-7300, IC-705, IC-9700, IC-7100 and more), Yaesu, Kenwood, Elecraft (KX2, KX3, K4), Xiegu, Lab599, GuoHe, FlexRadio, (tr)uSDX, FX-4CR, KN990, mcHF, Wolf SDR and QuantumSDR. Any other radio works through a VOX audio cable or a DigiRig.
- Network radios (experimental): TCI and FlexRadio SmartSDR, no cable and no sound card; the QRP Labs QMX can also be a receive-only I/Q receiver.
- SDR receivers (receive only): an RTL-SDR dongle on the phone's USB (the V3 and V4 included, no driver to install, bias tee switch), an RTL-SDR network server, KiwiSDR web receivers (yours or public), OpenHPSDR radios such as the Hermes-Lite 2, Red Pitaya, Airspy and others.
- The qFT8 bridge uses a radio connected to another of your devices, encrypted; the web remote lets a browser hear the radio and talk in SSB behind a private link and a password.

## Logging, services and events

- QSO syncing as you log: QRZ, Logbook of the World, eQSL, Club Log, HRDLog, HamQTH, World Radio League, HAMLOG.online, Wavelog, Cloudlog and qFT8log (one log shared between your own qFT8s). ADIF import and export. qFT8 never deletes a QSO on an online service.
- Logging programs on your network: the FT8 network log and ADIF over UDP, tested end to end with the common logging programs (named on qft8.com in the features list).
- Awards and activations: POTA and SOTA from the start (activate or hunt, count QSOs, spot yourself on POTA, export logs); experimental WWFF, WWBOTA, IOTA, SiOTA, HEMA, LLOTA, WWTOTA, RAZA, GMA and HOTA.
- Contests (experimental): ARRL Field Day, Winter Field Day, ARRL RTTY Roundup, ARRL International Digital Contest, FT Challenge and EU VHF, with the exchange, duplicate checks, the score and a Cabrillo export. AUTO is off where the rules forbid automated QSOs.
- Map and spots: a live world map of every station you hear with distance and bearing, PSK Reporter and WSPRnet spots (your decodes are reported too), propagation, POTA and SOTA activations, satellite tracks and a compass.

## Listening (SWL)

No callsign is needed. With an SDR or an ordinary radio qFT8 decodes every mode it knows, logs what it hears into a separate SWL log (QSOs and signals like ships, aircraft and time stations, with the receiver used), exports ADIF, CSV, SOTA SWL and RAZA SWL files, reports to eQSL (SWL account), PSK Reporter and WSPRnet, and has its own SWL tutorial. SWL and ham logs are never mixed. SWL awards give stars for the stations you hear (140 stars); HAM awards have 472.

## Languages

The app and this website are available in 63 languages (the app also has a British English spelling): the languages are listed below. The TX button's words (TX ON, TX OFF, TUNE) stay in English everywhere.

## Features in detail

### Modes

Weak-signal digital modes, keyboard chat, Morse, teletype, pictures and voice. Q65, MSK144, FST4, FST4W and JTTY are experimental.

FT8, FT4, FT2, LQ8, JS8, WSPR, Q65 (experimental), MSK144 (experimental), FST4 (experimental), FST4W (experimental), JT65 (experimental), JT9 (experimental), JT4 (experimental), CW, RTTY, JTTY (experimental), PSK31 (experimental), PSK63 (experimental), PSK125 (experimental), PSK250 (experimental), QPSK31 (experimental), QPSK63 (experimental), Olivia (experimental), MFSK16 (experimental), MFSK32 (experimental), MFSK64 (experimental), MFSK8 (experimental), MFSK11 (experimental), MFSK22 (experimental), MFSK128 (experimental), DominoEX (experimental), Feld Hell (experimental), THOR (experimental), Contestia (experimental), MT63 (experimental), Throb (experimental), IFKP (experimental), FSQ (experimental), SSTV, DRAW, SSB, AM

### Radios

Plug and play over USB with more than 70 radio models: qFT8 recognises the radio and sets up CAT and audio by itself. Any other radio works through a VOX audio cable or a DigiRig.

QRP Labs, Icom, Yaesu, Kenwood, Elecraft, Xiegu, Lab599, GuoHe, FlexRadio, (tr)uSDX, FX-4CR, KN990, mcHF, Wolf SDR, QuantumSDR

### SDR receivers and listening (SWL)

Listen without transmitting: an RTL-SDR dongle plugged into your phone or Linux computer (no driver to install, the V4 included), or over the network an RTL-SDR server, a KiwiSDR web receiver, a Hermes-Lite 2, an Airspy, an SDRplay and more. Every mode decodes as from a radio, and the QSOs you hear go to an SWL log with ADIF, SOTA SWL and RAZA SWL exports. Receive only.

RTL-SDR, KiwiSDR, OpenHPSDR, Hermes-Lite 2, Red Pitaya, Airspy / RTL-SDR server, remote SDR host, SWL, Airband (AM), Marine VHF (FM), FM + RDS (experimental), AM broadcast (experimental)

### Operating

Full AUTO answers CQs, runs the QSO and logs it, with retry limits you set; or call stations yourself with one tap. CW with on-screen paddles, keyboard and memories, SSB with voice memories, and transmit time limits that protect your radio.

Multi-tone (2 signals) (experimental)

### Award programmes

Hunt and activate: references on the map and in the station list, live spots, a QSO counter and ADIF exports. POTA and SOTA are on from the start; the others are experimental.

POTA, SOTA, WWFF (experimental), WWBOTA (experimental), IOTA (experimental), SiOTA (experimental), HEMA (experimental), LLOTA (experimental), WWTOTA (experimental), RAZA (experimental), GMA (experimental), HOTA (experimental)

### SWL support

No callsign needed: press SWL ONLY at the first start. What you hear is logged by itself in a heard (SWL) log, with the receiver it came through. Import and export it as ADIF or CSV, with SOTA and RAZA SWL files, send your reports to eQSL (SWL account), PSK Reporter and WSPRnet, and follow the built-in SWL tutorial. Receive only.

ADIF, CSV, eQSL, PSK Reporter, WSPRnet, SOTA SWL, RAZA SWL

### Signal receivers (SWL)

Receivers in the SWL tab for the signals around you, with an SDR or your radio: aircraft (ADS-B) and ships (AIS) live on the world map, LoRa and Meshtastic, digital-voice data (DMR, D-STAR, Fusion), HF data (ALE, ARDOP, PACTOR-I), FM with RDS and AM broadcast, weather and amateur satellites, radiosondes, time codes, weather fax and more. PROBE, the automatic mode detector, tells you what is on the air. Receive only.

ADS-B (experimental), AIS (experimental), LoRa (experimental), Meshtastic (experimental), ALE (experimental), ARDOP (experimental), PACTOR-I (experimental), FM RDS (experimental), AM (experimental), DMR (experimental), D-STAR (experimental), Fusion (experimental), APT (experimental), Meteor LRPT (experimental), Horus (experimental), RS41 (experimental), DCF77 (experimental), WWV (experimental), NAVTEX (experimental), DSC (experimental), APRS (experimental), VOR (experimental), ILS (experimental)

### Contests (experimental)

The exchange, duplicate checks, the score and a Cabrillo export. AUTO is switched off in the contests whose rules forbid automated QSOs.

ARRL Field Day (experimental), Winter Field Day (experimental), ARRL RTTY Roundup (experimental), ARRL International Digital Contest (experimental), FT Challenge (experimental), EU VHF (experimental)

### Online logbooks

Each QSO goes to the services you choose as you log it. qFT8log shares one log between your own qFT8s. ADIF import and export.

QRZ, Logbook of the World, eQSL, Club Log, HRDLog, HamQTH, World Radio League, HAMLOG.online, Wavelog, Cloudlog, qFT8log

### Logging programs on your network

FT8 network log and ADIF over UDP, both ways, plus the AC Log and DXLab interfaces (experimental). Tested with:

N1MM Logger+, Log4OM 2, N3FJP AC Log, CQRLOG, GridTracker, Wavelog, Cloudlog, qFT8log

### Map and spots

A live world map of every station you hear, with distance and bearing; spots from PSK Reporter and WSPRnet, LQ8 activity, POTA and SOTA activations, band propagation, satellite tracks and a map compass. Your own decodes are reported to PSK Reporter and WSPRnet.

### Anywhere

Remote control from any browser: hear the radio and talk in SSB, behind a private link and a password. Time from the internet or GPS, and it runs with the screen off.

## Questions and answers

### What is qFT8?

qFT8 is a free amateur radio program for weak-signal digital modes, Morse, teletype, pictures and voice. It runs on Android phones and tablets, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux, and can be controlled from any browser. It has no ads and needs no account. It is written by Luis Quesada Torres, HB9IPH, with its own decoders and encoders written from scratch.

### What is a good FT8 app for Android?

qFT8 is a complete FT8 station for Android 6.0 and newer, on phones and tablets: connect the radio with one USB cable and qFT8 recognises it and sets up CAT and audio by itself, with no computer and no interface box. It sends and receives FT8, FT4, FT2, LQ8, JS8, WSPR and more, answers CQs in full AUTO, keeps the clock right from the internet or GPS, shows every station on a live world map and logs each QSO to the services you choose. It keeps running with the screen off. Free, no ads, no account.

### Can I run FT8 on a Windows, Mac or Linux computer?

Yes. qFT8 runs on Windows (64-bit and 32-bit, also from the Microsoft Store), on every Mac (Apple Silicon and Intel) and on Linux (Intel/AMD and ARM, including the Raspberry Pi), with the same modes, radios and features as on Android. The downloads on this page are free.

### Is there an FT8 app for iPhone and iPad?

qFT8 also runs on iPhone and iPad (iOS). An iPhone or iPad cannot control a radio over a cable, so it keys the radio through the radio's VOX or through an audio interface that keys the radio from the audio.

### Which radios work with qFT8?

More than 70 radio models are plug and play over USB, among them the QRP Labs QMX, QMX+ and QDX, the Icom IC-7300, IC-705 and IC-9700, and radios from Yaesu, Kenwood, Elecraft, Xiegu, Lab599, GuoHe, FlexRadio and (tr)uSDX. Any other radio works through a VOX audio cable or a DigiRig, and SDR receivers such as an RTL-SDR can be used for receiving.

### Can I use a QRP Labs QMX or an Icom IC-7300 with my phone?

Yes. Plug the QMX, QMX+ or IC-7300 into an Android phone or tablet with one USB cable: qFT8 finds the radio, reads and sets its frequency over CAT, and sends and receives the audio over the same cable. No sound card or extra interface is needed. The same works with a computer.

### Which modes does qFT8 support?

FT8, FT4, FT2, LQ8, JS8, WSPR, CW, RTTY, SSTV and SSB, plus Q65, MSK144, FST4, FST4W, JT65, JT9, JT4, JTTY, PSK31, PSK63 and Olivia as experimental modes. LQ8 is a weak-signal mode created by HB9IPH that completes a QSO, with locator and signal report, in four messages.

### Does qFT8 work with POTA, SOTA, contests and online logbooks?

Yes. It shows POTA and SOTA references and live spots on the map and in the station list, counts your activation QSOs and exports ADIF; WWFF, IOTA, HEMA, GMA and other programmes, and contests such as ARRL Field Day, are experimental. Each QSO can go to QRZ, Logbook of the World, eQSL, Club Log, HRDLog, HamQTH, HAMLOG.online, Wavelog or Cloudlog as you log it, and to the logging programs on your network.

### Can I use qFT8 only to listen (SWL)?

Yes. qFT8 receives and decodes every mode it knows through an SDR receiver (an RTL-SDR dongle on an Android phone or a Linux computer, an RTL-SDR network server, your own or a public KiwiSDR, and other network SDRs) or through an ordinary radio in SWL mode, in which it never transmits. The QSOs you hear between other stations go to a heard log that exports SWL ADIF, CSV, SOTA SWL and RAZA SWL files. The user manual's SWL section explains the receivers and their drivers.

## Languages

The website is available in: English, Español, Português (Brasil), Português (Portugal), Français, Italiano, Deutsch, Русский, 简体中文, 繁體中文, 日本語, Esperanto, Română, हिन्दी, العربية, Català, Euskara, Galego, Bahasa Indonesia, 한국어, বাংলা, اردو, Tiếng Việt, Türkçe, Nederlands, Polski, Hausa, Čeština, Українська, Svenska, Suomi, Dansk, עברית, Magyar, Norsk, Slovenčina, ไทย, Srpski (latinica), Ελληνικά, Hrvatski, Български, Slovenščina, Lietuvių, Latviešu, Eesti, فارسی, Filipino, Македонски, Shqip, Bosanski, Беларуская, Қазақ тілі, ქართული, Հայերեն, Íslenska, Bahasa Melayu, Kiswahili, தமிழ், తెలుగు, मराठी, नेपाली, සිංහල, Монгол.
